slots.title: Brent up 1.0% on Saudi airport attacks
slots.body:
Brent crude closed at 101.57, up 1.0% in the latest commodity print.

CNBC linked the move to concern over Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia—airports in Jazan and Najran were targeted, according to the Saudi aviation authority.

That headline ran alongside talk of higher supply elsewhere in the Middle East; the story framed security worry as outweighing supply relief.

Brent’s session range in the data: 100.96 to 101.80.

Gold futures were 4,168.20, down 0.5%, in the same cross-asset panel.

Which matters more for your read on energy this week—shipping risk in the Gulf or official selling prices from producers?

slots.title: Three jobless prints tomorrow at 8:30
slots.body:
Three U.S. labor filings land tomorrow, Oct. 8, at 8:30 a.m.
ET.

Initial jobless claims: consensus 200K, prior week 197K.

Continuing claims (Sep. 26 week): estimate 1,710K, prior 1,701K.

Four-week average for initial claims: estimate 198K, prior 200K.

All three are flagged high impact on the calendar.

They measure how many people are newly filing for unemployment benefits and how many remain on rolls— a weekly pulse on layoffs, not the full monthly jobs report.

The last major jobs surprise in recent coverage was September payrolls well below expectations; these prints are the next frequent check on the labor side.

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 7, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished up 0.6% at 7,818.93, with an intraday high of 7,844.52 — matching the year high in the injected index data.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5% to 51,521.28.

The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.4% to 27,599.89, reaching an intraday high of 27,722.75, also the year high in the dataset.

Small caps diverged: the Russell 2000 fell 0.6% to 2,830.30.

The CBOE Volatility Index ($VIX) settled at 15.01, down 3.3% from the prior close of 15.52.

Sector leadership on Nasdaq was utilities at +3.0% average change, followed by consumer defensive (+1.6%), basic materials (+1.2%), and energy (+1.3%).

Healthcare was the weakest group at -1.5% average change; financial services and communication services were slightly negative, at about -0.2% and -0.5%.

Technology averaged -0.7% despite positive closes in several megacaps.

$AVGO led notable megcap gainers, up 3.7% to $375.81 on volume above 30 million shares.

$AMZN rose 1.9% to $256.29; $ORCL gained 1.6% to $144.76; $NFLX added 1.8% to $68.69; $PG rose 1.7% to $148.41.

$CRM fell 2.1% to $224.99; among heavily traded actives, $INTC was down 3.2% to $112.50.

$NVDA edged up 0.1% to $239.24, with an intraday high of $243.37 at the upper end of its 52-week range in the data.

Oil-linked assets firmed: Brent crude (BZUSD) was up 1.0% at $101.55; $USO closed up 0.6% at $144.91, in a session tied in news flow to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Gold futures (GCUSD) slipped 0.4% to $4,168.40.

The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund ($UUP) closed at $28.90, down 0.3%; EUR/USD was $1.12, down 0.3% in the forex quote.

Bitcoin ($BTCUSD) fell 1.7% to $84,061.47.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-10-05) show the 10-year at 5.3% and the 2s10s spread at 0.47 percentage points.

Overseas indexes in the dataset were mixed: Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.7%; the FTSE 100 rose 0.4%; the Hang Seng was down 0.7%.
